nodes.title: FINISHING
widgets_values:
FINISHING

AutoFinish builds the master automatically after the queue (RIFTCAST_AUDITION prefix here - rename per project). Judge results from the *_MASTER.mp4, never the in-canvas preview.

temporal_upscale 2x on Generate = ~48fps masters via the LTX temporal latent upsampler - audio untouched, 24fps render law preserved. Great on motion; skip it for dialogue close-ups and found-footage looks.

num_frames up to 1441 (60s) single take. 241 = 10s audition.

nodes.title: LORA STACK
widgets_values:
LORA STACK

ltx23_accent_american_v2 @ 1.0 - makes accent wording obeyable in the young-voice registers the base model ignores. Load-bearing; leave it at 1.0.

ltx23_surfaces_v1 @ 1.0 - always-on material realism (no trigger word). Grounds, walls, fabric, wear.

Chain another LoRA Stacker into this stacker's lora_stack input for character/style LoRAs. Everything fuses at load on safetensors DiT paths.

nodes.title: VOICES + REFERENCES
widgets_values:
VOICES + REFERENCES

Voice casting: a clip in input/joyecho_voices/<tag>/ makes every script with that speaker tag use that voice. RiftCast cartridges install these for you.

RefPicker scans the ACTIVE script text for names matching folders under your refs root and injects identity stills at shot 1 (no_reference = silently skip when nothing matches). In designer mode this means a PACKED character's re-auditions inherit their own face - continuity for free.

The LoadImage is only a manual fallback; leave it on example.png unless you want to force a specific reference.

{"prompts": ["Consumer mirrorless camera video, natural color, modest dynamic range, the storm light green-gray in the sky while skin tones and the red truck keep their true colors: a steady framing from the open passenger door of a pickup, medium framing on ID_A standing on the roadside ahead, her face and mouth fully visible, one continuous unbroken take that never cuts and never changes angle. The sky behind her is a low green-gray shelf cloud. The road is sun-bleached gray asphalt, its surface finely crazed like old porcelain, with one long sealed crack running away toward the horizon, and the wheat field beside it flattens in waves with each gust. The truck hood in the foreground is faded red paint dulled by years of sun, streaked with running rainwater, and every few seconds a single pea-sized hailstone strikes it with a sharp ping and skips away out of frame. ID_A is an American woman in her mid twenties with pale matte skin, visible pores, no makeup, long dark brown hair whipping across her face, wearing a heavy black raincoat open over a band tee. Her voice is a low American voice with a slight rasp, speaking in a casual American accent, fast and thrilled, and she keeps talking through everything that happens. Pointing at the sky she shouts, \"Okay okay okay, THAT is rotation, do you see that? That whole shelf is turning like a plate!\" Hail comes harder, single stones striking the asphalt around her boots and skipping away, and she whoops and yells, \"It's hailing sideways, this is the best day of my entire life!\" She sprints for the truck, dives into the seat laughing, drags the door shut, and shouts over the drumming, \"Nope, nope, we're done, roll the windows up!\" as hail hammers the windshield in the final seconds. Her lips move naturally in tight sync with every word. She is the only person in frame and hers is the only voice on the track. The only sounds are wind roar, hail pinging off steel and asphalt, her boots on the road, the door slam, and her voice shouting close on the mic."]}
packed EMMA.riftcast (120 anchor frames, 3 refs) and installed - speaker tag 'emma' casts in the next render. Re-queue the audition with a new seed to recast; delete the .riftcast to retire.

nodes.title: READ ME - THE 24 FPS LAW
widgets_values:
READ ME - THE 24 FPS LAW

video_fps stays at 24. Always.

LTX-2.3's joint audio-video prior is 24fps-native and fps is a hidden ACCENT dial: 25fps drifts every voice to southern British, 30fps to broad Australian - and off-24 overrides accent wording in your prompt entirely. Verified by A/B with blind phonetic review.

Want a British/Australian character on purpose? Render THEIR scenes at 25/30. Otherwise: 24, say the accent in the prompt, keep the accent v2 LoRA at 1.0.

nodes.title: TWO MODES - THE SOURCE SWITCH
widgets_values:
TWO MODES - THE SOURCE SWITCH

The RiftCast Source Switch picks what drives this queue:

PROMPT FILE - classic batch rendering. Point PromptSource at any LPFF txt or script JSON; easy-seed sets the block index.

CHARACTER DESIGNER - set the dropdowns, queue, and the character records an audition tape. The Packer cuts their voice anchor + 3 reference stills from that render and installs NAME.riftcast automatically. Re-queue with a new seed to recast; delete the file in input/riftcast/ to retire them.

Cartridges also auto-install at startup: drop any .riftcast into input/riftcast/ and just mention the character in a script.

Consumer mirrorless camera video, neutral color, modest dynamic range, slight sensor noise crawl in the shadows: a locked static medium shot in a small casting room, framed from the waist up with the bottom edge of frame crossing just above the hips, one continuous unbroken take that never cuts and never changes angle. The backdrop is matte gray seamless paper with a soft vertical curl at its edge, taped at the top corners, the paper catching the key as a flat diffuse expanse with no specular sheen. The light is one large soft key from the front, even and flattering, falling diffusely with no hard specular catch, the shadows soft and shallow. {dna} Looking into the lens, calm and personable, {name} rests both forearms on {pos} thighs so the hands come up into the bottom of frame, then partway through settles back, {pos} shoulders dropping as an exhale crosses {pos} face that almost becomes a smile. {name} brings one hand up to tuck a strand of hair behind {pos} ear, lets it fall, and as the take ends the easy expression drops a fraction then returns smaller and real. {name} is talking, saying in a {accent} accent, "{dialogue}" {pos_cap} lips move naturally in tight sync with every word. {name} is the only person in frame and {pos} voice is the only voice on the audio track. The only sounds are the room's quiet air, a faint camera-handling sound at the start, fabric shifting as {pos} shoulders settle, a single quiet creak from the seat, and {pos} voice close and clean on the mic.

Hi, my name's {name_title}. This is my audition tape, so, here's a little about how I sound when I'm just talking. I can dial it either direction, no problem. Straight commercial read, character work, voiceover, whatever you need. I'll read whatever you've got, whenever you're ready. Thanks for watching!
a bold red lip and nothing else
restless, shifting and gesturing while talking
